title: Transforming blood-derived episignatures into cell-type-agnostic classifiers: A shortcut to prenatal episignatures.
data_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ (public Down syndrome methylation-array series, e.g. GSE52588, GSE66210, GSE74486; the paper's exact list was not retrievable)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Paper has no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement in Europe PMC. Searched GEO: 39 human Down syndrome/trisomy 21 methylation series. Opened sample metadata for three: GSE52588 (87 blood: 29 Down syndrome, 29 siblings, 29 mothers), GSE66210 (46 chorionic villus + 14 maternal blood; 14 trisomy 21 pregnancies, 12 trisomy 18), GSE74486 (131 brain/blood; 70 Down syndrome, 58 normal). Labels sit in a 'disease state'/'pregnancy' field. GSE52588 series matrix is 175 MB (HEAD only, not downloaded, over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 266-sample blood cohort, the 850 public samples across six tissues, and the claim of accurate trisomy 21 prediction in all tissues come from the abstract only. Which GEO series make up the 850, and whether the 266-sample cohort is deposited anywhere, are unknown.

a1_downloadable.note: The public half (GEO methylation-array series) downloads without login; checked metadata for 3 series. The 266-sample blood cohort is probably the authors' clinical cohort; I found no deposit.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Trisomy 21 status is a GEO sample field ('disease state: Down syndrome', 'pregnancy: trisomy 21'), seen in files. Wording differs between series, so it needs a small manual mapping.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are methylation beta values (fraction of DNA copies methylated at each CpG site, 0 to 1) in GEO series matrices; HEAD only, not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Beta values are a standard 0–1 scale from Illumina 450K/EPIC arrays; processing differs by submitter (taken from GEO convention, not checked in the files).

a5_enough_rows.note: The abstract says 850 public samples; I counted 264 across 3 series. Classification needs about 400 rows, which is met overall, but prenatal trisomy 21 samples are few (14 chorionic villus in GSE66210).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1-2 GB of gzipped series matrices; subset to a few thousand CpG sites, which is far under 1 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: About 850 × 450k float32 values is ~1.5 GB in memory before subsetting; the files are bigger than the 50 MB fetch cap, so they were not downloaded.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts can't be fully checked without the paper's list of series. The 3 series I opened match their GEO descriptions.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is a karyotype (chromosome count) diagnosis made clinically, independently of the methylation measurement, so it is not circular.

B1.why: About 6-10 separate GEO series, each with its own matrix and its own metadata wording (seen in metadata).

B2.why: GEO series matrices parse in a standard way, but some series give only raw IDAT files; not opened.

B3.why: Arrays from different labs and normalisations (450K vs EPIC); batch effects line up with tissue and series.

B4.why: Binary karyotype label; there are no censored values.

B5.why: Some series overlap (GSE74519 is a superseries containing GSE74486), so samples must be deduplicated by sample ID (GSM).

B6.why: GEO fields are self-explanatory but not standardised across series.

C1.why: The paper already reports accurate trisomy 21 prediction in all six tissues; replicating it adds little.

C2.why: This paper's cross-tissue classifier exists; code and weights were not found; full text unavailable to check splits.

C3.why: Trisomy 21 is the authors' proof-of-concept; the real target (rare-disorder episignatures) needs the controlled EpiSign data.

C4.why: Trisomy 21 is already diagnosed cheaply and definitively by karyotype, microarray or prenatal cell-free DNA screening.

C5.why: The abstract says 'accurate' without a number I could retrieve; the dummy is the majority class.

D1.why: Methylation foundation models (e.g. CpGPT) exist but I didn't verify their weights or licence; none of the standard backbones fits.

D2.why: A penalised logistic regression or SVM (support vector machine) on beta values is the natural model; a backbone isn't needed.

D3.why: Licence unclear for methylation foundation models; the GEO data itself is open.

E1.why: A leave-one-tissue-out or leave-one-series-out split is possible from the GEO metadata.

E2.why: Six tissues and at least 6 series, according to the abstract and the GEO search.

E4.why: No replicate arrays seen; the karyotype label is effectively noise-free.

E5.why: Known chromosome 21 and genome-wide methylation shifts in Down syndrome; predicting sex from X-chromosome CpG sites is a trivial control.

E6.why: Label shuffling and dropping the chromosome 21 CpG sites are both straightforward.

E7.why: Independent tissues and series act as external sets; trisomy 18 samples in GSE66210 test specificity.

E8.why: No full text, so the paper's numbers and splits can't be reproduced.

G1.why: Illumina CpG probe IDs map to genomic coordinates (hg19).

G2.why: Other GEO methylation sets or the EpiSign knowledge base, which is controlled access.

G3.why: Arrays join on probe ID, one-to-one.

G4.why: The bigger question (prenatal rare-disorder episignatures) needs data that isn't public.

H1.why: Control samples are present in every series checked (58 normal in GSE74486, 28 normal pregnancies in GSE66210).

H2.why: Several labs and tissues, but each tissue comes mostly from one series, so tissue and lab are confounded.

H3.why: The claim can be stated precisely; see honest_claim_h3.

H4.why: Small prenatal sample sizes are stated in the abstract; the confounding between tissue and batch is not.

I1.why: Episignature diagnostic labs (EpiSign at London Health Sciences, SickKids).

I2.why: Trisomy 21 detection by methylation won't change any clinical decision; karyotype already settles it.

I3.why: Classification accuracy matches a diagnosis, but trisomy 21 is not a decision anyone needs a model for.

I4.why: Counting chromosome 21 copies, or a simple methylation threshold, likely separates the classes almost perfectly.

J1.why: Mostly harmonising data across GEO series; little modelling.

J2.why: The result is easy to sanity-check, because the classes separate so well.

J3.why: A cross-tissue transfer table is shareable, but it largely duplicates the paper.

existing_models.name: This paper's cross-tissue trisomy 21 episignature classifier
existing_models.score_and_split: The abstract says 'accurate prediction of T21 status across all tested tissues'; numbers and split not retrievable (no open full text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Extending this to rare-disorder episignatures where prenatal samples are scarce.

existing_models.name: EpiSign (commercial clinical episignature SVM classifier, blood only)
existing_models.score_and_split: Clinical report: 312 of 1,667 comprehensively screened cases (18.7%) positive; proprietary database.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Restricted data sharing limits building episignatures for more disorders.

backbone.name: None standard; a methylation foundation model (e.g. CpGPT) is possible but its weights and licence are unverified
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop is enough for a penalised linear model or SVM
backbone.licence: GEO data open; backbone licence unknown

integration.partner_dataset: Other public GEO methylation-array series of Down syndrome and of other aneuploidies (e.g. the trisomy 13 and 18 samples in GSE66210)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a methylation signature learned in blood carry over to placenta and fetal tissue for disorders other than aneuploidy? Answering that needs controlled-access rare-disease data.

controls.positive_control: Predict sex from X-chromosome CpG sites, and recover the known chromosome 21 methylation shifts in Down syndrome.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the labels; shuffle within each tissue; leave out one series to expose batch leakage.
controls.external_validation: A held-out tissue or GEO series; trisomy 18 and 13 chorionic villus samples as a specificity check.

honest_claim_h3: Among public array samples from a handful of labs, a methylation classifier trained on some tissues detects trisomy 21 in a held-out tissue. The paper already reports this, and karyotyping diagnoses it anyway.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA methylation measured in one tissue to detect Down syndrome in other tissues, including prenatal samples.
plain_idea.train_on: Methylation levels at about 450,000 DNA sites for each public sample; the abstract says 850 samples across six tissues; I counted 264 in three series.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the sample carries an extra chromosome 21 (Down syndrome). The true answer comes from the clinical karyotype, recorded in the GEO metadata.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Only as a test of whether blood-derived methylation signatures transfer to other tissues; Down syndrome itself is already diagnosed cheaply, so little would change for anyone.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use the same public GEO samples the paper used (850), minus its 266-sample blood cohort.

confidence_score.why: With near-perfect class separation, confidence estimates add nothing useful.

models_beatable.why: The 2026 paper already reports accurate prediction in all six tissues; there is little room above that.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The paper's model isn't available to run as a baseline, and no new data that joins measures the same thing on more prenatal samples.

label_elsewhere.sources: Other GEO Down syndrome methylation series (found by searching GEO: 39 series); the EpiSign knowledge base is controlled access.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Illumina CpG probe ID / GEO sample ID (GSM)
label_elsewhere.why: More trisomy 21 samples exist, but they are spread across small series from different labs, which limits them as clean external tests.

ml_idea: Leave-one-tissue-out penalised logistic regression or SVM on harmonised GEO 450K/EPIC beta values to classify trisomy 21, with chromosome 21 ablation and leave-one-series-out checks for batch leakage.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: about 850 samples × a few thousand selected CpG sites; harmonising several GEO series and their metadata dominates the time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the prenatal trisomy 21 samples per tissue across the GEO series; if fewer than about 20 per tissue, transfer results won't be stable.

verdict_reason: Part A passes on the public GEO half, but the question fails: the paper already shows trisomy 21 is detectable in all six tissues, karyotyping already diagnoses it cheaply, and the target that would matter (rare-disorder episignatures) needs controlled-access EpiSign data.
